question: What enzyme do the kidneys release when blood pressure drops too low?

options.A: Renin
options.B: Amylase
options.C: Pepsin
options.D: Lipase

explanation: You've got this! Specialized cells in the kidney release renin to start a chain reaction that brings blood pressure back up where it belongs.

question: What is the primary benefit of connecting a newly diagnosed patient to a peer support group?

options.A: It normalizes their experience and shows them that people can live long, healthy lives with HIV
options.B: It cures the viral infection within a few weeks of consistent meetings
options.C: It provides them with free housing and government food supplies
options.D: It legally waives their responsibility to ever inform their sexual partners

explanation: Peer groups reduce feelings of isolation by introducing patients to others who are thriving despite their diagnosis. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: How should a freshly applied Plaster of Paris cast be supported while it dries?

options.A: Covered tightly with heavy warm blankets to trap heat
options.B: Suspended vertically by a rope attached to the ceiling
options.C: Lying directly flat on a hard wooden examination table
options.D: Resting on soft pillows with open air circulation

explanation: Soft pillows cradle the wet cast and support its shape without pressing flat, damaging spots into the drying plaster.

question: Why do patients with chronic renal failure frequently look very pale and complain of severe tiredness?

options.A: The liver stops producing enough protein to carry vitamins.
options.B: Decreased erythropoietin production leads to anemia.
options.C: Excess sodium in the blood blocks oxygen from entering the lungs.
options.D: High potassium levels destroy red blood cells in the bloodstream.

explanation: Remember, damaged kidneys forget to make enough erythropoietin—the hormone that tells your bone marrow to build red blood cells. Without it, anemia sets in!

question: A pregnant home-care patient has a single high blood pressure reading. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all prescribed prenatal vitamins.
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient from home care services.
options.C: Perform serial blood pressure checks and notify the primary provider.
options.D: Wait until the scheduled monthly clinic visit to mention it.

explanation: A single high reading needs re-checking to confirm a trend, and the provider must be informed promptly to rule out gestational hypertension. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h3)

question: Why does fluid naturally collect in the Pouch of Douglas when there is pelvic bleeding or infection?

options.A: It is the lowest point of the female pelvic cavity.
options.B: It has high muscular pressure that pushes fluid down.
options.C: It connects directly to the urinary bladder.
options.D: It actively secretes lubricating fluid into the pelvis.

explanation: Think of gravity! Because this pouch is the deepest pocket in the female pelvis, any free fluid naturally flows and pools right down there.

question: Looking at these patient groups, who needs the highest amount of protein relative to their body weight?

options.A: Healthy young adults walking for thirty minutes daily
options.B: Patients recovering from severe burns or trauma
options.C: Sedentary office workers with desk jobs
options.D: Elderly individuals resting quietly in bed

explanation: Trauma and burns create a massive healing demand. These patients need significantly more protein to rebuild their damaged tissues.

question: Your patient is medically ready to leave the clinic, but is terrified to go back to an unsafe home. What should you do?

options.A: Advise the patient to ignore the fear and return home immediately
options.B: Connect the patient with safe shelter and social welfare referral services
options.C: Contact law enforcement to arrest the patient for missing work
options.D: Discharge the patient without discussing housing or safety plans

explanation: Never send a vulnerable patient back into danger. Connecting them with safe housing and social workers is a lifesaver.

question: Why do pregnant women and young children get severe malaria so easily in Nigeria?

options.A: Their immune defenses are either developing or temporarily lowered
options.B: They have a naturally higher body temperature that attracts vectors
options.C: They spend more time outdoors during peak sunlight hours
options.D: Their diets lack the specific nutrients required to fight protozoa

explanation: You got it! Little ones are still building their immune defenses, and pregnancy naturally lowers a woman's immune response for a bit, making them extra vulnerable.

question: What does a sudden, unexpected drop in the remaining volume of medication usually mean?

options.A: That the patient is metabolizing the drug much faster than usual
options.B: That the medication has expired inside the syringe barrel
options.C: A potential mechanical issue or free-flow of medication
options.D: Normal operation of the machine battery charging cycle

explanation: Spot on! If fluid disappears way too fast, stop and check right away for line leaks, programming errors, or accidental free-flowing.

question: A patient has been vomiting nonstop for three days. Which blood lab imbalance should the nurse expect?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic acidosis

explanation: Brilliant! Throwing up all that stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) leaves the body with extra bicarbonate, pushing the blood into metabolic alkalosis. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: What should you teach a patient about how fast anticholinergics start working for overactive bladder?

options.A: Relief happens within ten minutes of the first dose
options.B: It may take a few weeks to notice full therapeutic effects
options.C: Effects only appear after finishing the entire prescription
options.D: Results are immediate on the very first day of use

explanation: Patients might feel discouraged if it doesn't work on day one. Letting them know it takes a couple of weeks helps keep them taking their meds.

question: Why is talking about birth control early in post-abortion care so crucial?

options.A: Birth control pills must be taken to prevent future ectopic pregnancies
options.B: Ovulation can return as early as two weeks after the procedure
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop ongoing uterine bleeding
options.D: Patients lose natural fertility permanently after a medication abortion

explanation: A patient can actually get pregnant again before their next normal period even arrives, so early counseling is a lifesaver.

question: Who typically performs the gishiri cut procedure in rural communities?

options.A: Trained midwives
options.B: Traditional healers
options.C: Public health nurses
options.D: General surgeons

explanation: Local practitioners and traditional birth attendants without formal medical training perform these cuts based on cultural beliefs. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h1)

question: How does teamwork between nurses, doctors, and pharmacists improve the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: By removing the need for any internal hospital quality audits
options.B: By allowing nurses to take over surgical operations from physicians
options.C: By shifting all financial responsibilities entirely onto patients
options.D: By combining different professional skills to prevent drug errors and waste

explanation: Spot on! When healthcare professionals team up, they catch mistakes early and keep patients safe.

question: Why do people trying to quit smoking often get sudden cravings when doing routine things, like drinking morning tea?

options.A: Their physical lungs are suddenly damaged by the beverage steam
options.B: The brain has formed strong behavioral links between those routines and smoking
options.C: Their immune system is reacting to dietary changes
options.D: The tea contains hidden traces of chemical nicotine

explanation: Daily habits act as triggers because the brain links those routines directly to smoking. Recognizing this helps us support patients better!

question: A patient in the intensive care unit is being evaluated for potential brain death. Which test is routinely used to confirm this?

options.A: Electroencephalography
options.B: Lumbar puncture
options.C: Barium swallow study
options.D: Electromyography

explanation: When doctors need to check for remaining brain activity in severe cases, a completely flatline EEG (cerebral silence) helps confirm brain death.

question: What is one of the very early physical signs of pregnancy you might spot on a woman's breasts due to extra blood flow?

options.A: Shrinkage of the overall breast size
options.B: Complete absence of areolar pigmentation
options.C: Prominent and visible superficial veins
options.D: Active secretion of mature white milk

explanation: Because the body sends extra blood to the breasts to prepare for feeding, the veins near the surface become much easier to see. Neat physiological adaptation, right?

question: How does a newborn's very first breath instantly change blood flow in the heart?

options.A: It causes blood to back up into the superior vena cava from the lungs
options.B: It increases pressure in the right atrium to force the ductus open wider
options.C: It lowers pulmonary resistance, encouraging blood to flow into the lungs
options.D: It stops blood from returning to the right side of the heart entirely

explanation: Amazing! When air rushes into the baby's lungs for the first time, the blood vessels inside open right up. This makes it super easy for blood to flow in and pick up oxygen.

question: A mother calls because her 2-day-old baby is super sleepy and won't feed at all. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.A: A mild milk allergy needing a brand change
options.B: Normal newborn behavior that will fix itself
options.C: A serious hidden problem needing urgent medical review
options.D: Just normal tiredness from growing

explanation: Lethargy and refusing to feed are major warning signs in babies. It could point to infection, low blood sugar, or dehydration—always treat it as urgent!

question: What is the main job of muscle spindles?

options.A: To measure the amount of tension placed on a tendon
options.B: To stop muscles from contracting when they get too tired
options.C: To provide energy for the muscle cells during hard work
options.D: To monitor changes in muscle length and stretch speed

explanation: Muscle spindles act like tiny built-in stretch detectors inside your muscles, keeping track of how fast and how far the muscle is stretching.

question: What does your skin do when you step into a cold environment?

options.A: Blood vessels in the skin widen to let heat out
options.B: Sweat glands release extra cooling fluid
options.C: Melanocytes produce more dark pigment
options.D: Blood vessels in the skin narrow to hold in body heat

explanation: Well done! When it's cold, your blood vessels squeeze shut near the surface to keep your warm blood safely around your inner organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)

question: How do Volkmann's canals differ in direction from Haversian canals?

options.A: Volkmann's run horizontally, while Haversian run vertically
options.B: Volkmann's are microscopic, while Haversian are visible to the eye
options.C: Volkmann's are found in spongy bone, while Haversian are in compact bone
options.D: Volkmann's carry nerves only, while Haversian carry blood only

explanation: Spot on! Volkmann's run across horizontally, linking up nicely with the vertical central (Haversian) canals inside the osteons.

question: Why is keeping track of information so important for UNOCHA during a major disaster?

options.A: It prevents duplication of relief efforts and identifies gaps in aid delivery
options.B: It replaces the need for local health assessments by foreign doctors
options.C: It allows the agency to control all financial transactions in the host country
options.D: It guarantees that political leaders will fund the recovery process

explanation: Exactly! By tracking who is doing what, we make sure food and medicine reach every community without wasting supplies or leaving anyone out.

question: Why is family caregiver education such a vital part of home health nursing?

options.A: Caregivers are legally required to pass nursing board examinations
options.B: Caregivers handle daily care routines during the many hours professionals are absent
options.C: Physicians require family members to sign off on all medical orders
options.D: Education allows family members to replace paid aides entirely

explanation: Because healthcare staff are only present briefly, family caregivers must be taught how to manage routines safely when alone. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a comprehensive community diagnosis?

options.A: A financial audit of local government health clinics
options.B: An in-depth study covering all aspects of health and life in the community
options.C: A quick check of only the children under five years old
options.D: A laboratory test for a single infectious disease

explanation: A comprehensive diagnosis looks at everything from demographics and economics to all available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: What actually happens when someone has a physical dependence on a drug?

options.A: The complete inability to remember recent events after drinking
options.B: A sudden allergy to chemical substances found in prescription drugs
options.C: The body reacts with unpleasant symptoms when the drug is stopped
options.D: An emotional desire to feel happy without taking any medicine

explanation: Spot on! Physical dependence simply means the body has gotten so used to the drug that it protests with withdrawal signs when the supply cuts off. You've got this!

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It can only be performed on hospitalized surgical patients
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to analyze
options.C: It measures body fat percentage instead of food intake
options.D: It relies heavily on the patient's memory and honesty

explanation: Patients can easily forget what they ate or misjudge portion sizes, which can make your dietary data a bit off.

question: What makes a malignant tumor much more dangerous than a benign one?

options.A: Their tendency to cause severe local pain within days of starting
options.B: The fact that they always grow much larger than benign lumps
options.C: The complete absence of blood vessels inside their tissue mass
options.D: The ability to invade nearby structures and spread to distant organs

explanation: Malignant cells are troublemakers because they don't stay put. They love to break away and travel to other parts of the body.

question: Which part of the nerve cell is mainly destroyed during the demyelination process in disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Gray matter neurons
options.C: Myelin sheath
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: You've got this! The immune system mistakenly attacks and strips away the myelin sheath, which normally acts like an insulation cover to protect nerves and speed up signals.

question: Which type of wound is created under clean, controlled hospital conditions?

options.A: Contaminated laceration
options.B: Traumatic abrasion
options.C: Intentional wound
options.D: Infected ulcer

explanation: An intentional wound is just a planned surgical cut made by a surgeon using strict sterile steps. Nice and straightforward!

question: Which of these is considered the most serious complication of an endoscopy?

options.A: Mild throat irritation from the tube
options.B: Perforation of the organ wall
options.C: Passing gas shortly after waking up
options.D: Temporary drowsiness from sedation

explanation: A tear (perforation) in the gut wall is a serious emergency because it can let bacteria leak into the body, requiring immediate medical care.

question: Which common test is used to tell Staphylococcus and Streptococcus apart?

options.A: Acid-fast test
options.B: Gram stain test
options.C: Catalase test
options.D: Capsule staining test

explanation: Great work! Staph makes an enzyme called catalase that bubbles up when you add hydrogen peroxide, but strep doesn't.

question: What is the main goal of getting widespread COVID-19 vaccinations?

options.A: Prevention of all future bacterial lung infections
options.B: Prevention of severe disease, hospitalization, and death
options.C: Complete eradication of all human coronaviruses worldwide
options.D: Immediate elimination of the need for hand washing

explanation: Vaccines help train your immune system so that even if you catch the virus, you are much less likely to get severely sick or end up in the hospital. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h8)

question: During a sudden emergency on the ward, the charge nurse gives quick, direct orders without debating. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-Faire
options.C: Autocratic
options.D: Transformational

explanation: In an emergency, there's no time for a committee meeting! An autocratic style gives fast, clear direction when every second counts.

question: What is the standard diagnostic test used to confirm onchocerciasis?

options.A: Chest X-ray imaging
options.B: Bone marrow biopsy
options.C: Stool microscopy for ova
options.D: Skin snip microscopy

explanation: Taking small skin snips and observing the crawling microfilariae under a microscope remains the standard diagnostic method. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of purposive sampling in qualitative studies?

options.A: Choosing people randomly from a large national census list
options.B: Ensuring every person in the hospital has an equal chance to join
options.C: Selecting participants who have direct experience with the topic
options.D: Finding participants who disagree with the researcher's hypothesis

explanation: Exactly! 'Purposive' means on purpose—you pick people who actually lived the experience so they can give you the best information.

question: Why is teaching patients how to avoid environmental hazards so important after an insect sting recovery?

options.A: It guarantees that insect populations will decrease around the home
options.B: It eliminates the patient's biological sensitivity to insect venom
options.C: It minimizes the chance of future exposure and repeat anaphylactic events
options.D: It replaces the need to carry emergency rescue medications

explanation: Prevention is key! Simple steps like wearing protective clothes keep patients out of harm's way so they don't experience another scary reaction.

question: How should a nurse position a patient experiencing Superior Vena Cava Syndrome to help ease their symptoms?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillow
options.B: With their legs raised higher than their head
options.C: On their left side in the recovery position
options.D: Upright with the head elevated

explanation: Keeping the head of the bed elevated uses gravity to help reduce venous pressure and swelling in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why do we encourage variety when planning daily meals?

options.A: It helps prevent eating too much of any single nutrient
options.B: It guarantees that food costs will remain very low
options.C: It ensures the body burns fat twice as fast
options.D: It removes the need to drink water with meals

explanation: Great job! Eating a nice mix of different foods keeps you from relying on just one thing, lowering the risk of missing out on some nutrients or overloading on another.

question: Which of the following is a common operational barrier to implementing clinical standards in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Shortages of essential equipment and supplies
options.B: A complete absence of hospital patients
options.C: Too much free time during morning shifts
options.D: An excess of available nursing personnel on every shift

explanation: Without basic tools like gloves, clean water, or drugs, nurses struggle to follow clinical standards properly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is a major goal of skilled care when looking after someone with a long-term, chronic illness?

options.A: Elimination of all daily living assistance needs.
options.B: Complete permanent cure of the underlying disease.
options.C: Immediate discharge back to independent living.
options.D: Stabilization, symptom relief, and functional preservation.

explanation: When a chronic condition can't be cured, our goal shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and helping them stay as active as possible.

question: How do digital technologies help modern health maintenance agencies do their jobs better?

options.A: They prevent all infectious diseases from ever occurring again
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any human nurses
options.C: They replace the need for clean water and sanitation programs
options.D: They enable real-time electronic disease surveillance and faster responses

explanation: Spot on! Digital tools and electronic tracking help agencies spot outbreaks instantly, replacing slow paper files with lightning-fast updates.

question: Why is malaria considered an endemic disease in Nigeria?

options.A: Because transmission cycles happen year-round without stopping
options.B: Because it causes sudden outbreaks only during the harmattan season
options.C: Because the federal government eradicated it completely last year
options.D: Because it only affects individuals who travel outside the country

explanation: Malaria remains present at predictable, steady rates in Nigeria throughout the entire year, which is the exact definition of an endemic disease.

question: A patient taking high-dose prednisone for six months reports feeling very hungry all the time and notices weight gain around the face and neck. What causes this?

options.A: Fluid is building up inside the brain tissue.
options.B: Steroids alter how the body stores fat and stimulates appetite.
options.C: The medication is destroying the thyroid gland completely.
options.D: The patient is secretly eating too much junk food at night.

explanation: Corticosteroids alter carbohydrate and fat metabolism, frequently causing increased appetite and fat redistribution. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h5)

question: How does involving local residents in a community diagnosis help public health programs?

options.A: It builds local ownership and cooperation for the health programs
options.B: It shifts all financial responsibility entirely onto the villagers
options.C: It ensures that no diseases will ever reappear in the community
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to collect any data themselves

explanation: Spot on! When community members are part of identifying their challenges, they are much more willing to embrace and support the solutions.

question: What is the best way to help prevent teenage pregnancies at the community level?

options.A: Mandatory curfews enforced by police officers
options.B: Banning teenagers from using public transportation
options.C: Comprehensive sexuality education and youth-friendly health services
options.D: Isolating pregnant teens from community activities

explanation: You nailed it! Giving young people clear health education and easy access to friendly, welcoming clinics helps them make safe choices.

question: What do we call a patient who keeps shedding germs even after they've started feeling better?

options.A: Incubation carrier
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Acute clinical case
options.D: Convalescent carrier

explanation: A convalescent carrier is someone who is recovering and feeling good again, but their body is still letting out a few leftover germs.

question: Which of the following is an early physical sign of significant blood loss?

options.A: A fast heart rate
options.B: Flushed, warm skin
options.C: A very slow pulse
options.D: High urine output

explanation: The heart beats faster to pump the remaining blood volume harder and maintain cardiac output when blood is lost. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h3)

question: What is the most important first step when a patient rings the bell asking for nausea medication?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water
options.B: Immediately administer a broad-spectrum 5-HT3 antagonist IV
options.C: Assess the character, frequency, and potential triggers of the nausea
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Always assess first before giving meds. Understanding what's causing the nausea helps you pick the right treatment and catch hidden dangers. Excellent nursing judgment!

question: Why is the inner forearm a preferred site for routine tuberculosis skin tests?

options.A: It is hairless and allows easy visual inspection of the reaction.
options.B: It has a higher concentration of blood vessels for rapid results.
options.C: It contains thick subcutaneous fat that cushions the needle.
options.D: It absorbs medications much faster than other body parts.

explanation: The inner forearm provides a clear, accessible area with minimal hair, making it simple for nurses to read skin changes accurately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the standard baseline daily protein recommendation (RDA) for a healthy, less active adult?

options.A: 10 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.B: 5.0 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.C: 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight
options.D: 2.5 grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: 0.8 grams per kg is the golden baseline set to keep a healthy adult from deficiency and maintain a steady nitrogen balance. Easy to remember for your exams!

question: A client calls the clinic to say she missed one active combination pill today. What should you advise her to do?

options.A: Take the missed pill immediately and continue as normal
options.B: Wait until tomorrow and take three pills at once
options.C: Throw away the rest of the month and start a new pack
options.D: Stop taking the pack entirely and wait for her next menses

explanation: Don't panic over one missed pill! Just take the forgotten pill right away and keep going with your normal schedule to stay protected.

question: What is the big advantage of using open-ended questions?

options.A: They provide quick, exact "yes" or "no" answers
options.B: They encourage the patient to share a detailed narrative
options.C: They eliminate the need for active listening entirely
options.D: They prevent the patient from talking too much

explanation: Spot on! Open questions let patients tell their story in their own words, giving you much better insight.

question: What is the main focus of a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Meeting the social needs of the nursing staff
options.B: Building a long-lasting personal friendship
options.C: The health needs and well-being of the patient
options.D: Completing hospital paperwork as fast as possible

explanation: Well done! Unlike regular friendships, therapeutic relationships are completely focused on helping the patient get better.

question: When health systems face a 'double burden of disease', what two types of health challenges are they dealing with?

options.A: Surgical trauma and genetic deformities
options.B: Acute poisoning and chronic malnutrition
options.C: Communicable and non-communicable illnesses
options.D: Pediatric and geriatric psychological disorders

explanation: Nailed it! It means fighting infectious diseases (like malaria) while also managing lifestyle conditions (like hypertension) at the same time.

question: What makes the enteric nervous system so special compared to other parts of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: It receives no innervation whatsoever from the sympathetic division.
options.B: It can direct gut functions largely on its own without central nervous system input.
options.C: It controls voluntary swallowing in the upper esophagus.
options.D: It is the only part of the nervous system that uses acetylcholine.

explanation: Even though it chats with the brain, the enteric nervous system has its own local reflex circuits and can run digestion completely on autopilot!

question: Which body language shows a supportive and comforting style to a nervous patient?

options.A: Standing over the bed to show clinical dominance
options.B: Staring intently at the medical chart while the patient speaks
options.C: Crossing arms firmly across the chest to establish authority
options.D: Maintaining a calm tone and open, welcoming body language

explanation: A gentle voice and open posture tell the patient 'I am here for you, and you are safe with me.'

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is for chronic diseases, while quarantine is for acute injuries
options.B: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation uses physical barriers only
options.C: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.D: There is no difference; the terms mean the exact same thing

explanation: Easy to remember: Isolation is for those already sick, while quarantine is for healthy folks who were exposed and need to be watched.

question: What is the main job of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To connect the central nervous system to the rest of the body
options.B: To produce vital brain chemicals
options.C: To store long-term memories in the brain
options.D: To protect the delicate spinal cord from physical injury

explanation: You got it! Think of the peripheral nervous system as the network of highways carrying messages back and forth between your brain/spinal cord and your limbs.

question: Why is timely documentation of assessment findings important for patient care?

options.A: It is only required for billing and insurance purposes
options.B: It prevents patients from reading their own medical charts
options.C: It ensures continuity of care and accurate communication across shifts
options.D: It allows the nurse to leave the hospital premises much earlier

explanation: Prompt charting lets the next nurse or doctor know the exact status of the patient without relying on memory. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on a sedated patient such an important nursing duty?

options.A: The effect of sedatives exists on a sliding scale from calm to dangerous coma
options.B: Patients develop permanent neurological damage after a single dose
options.C: Medication clearance happens instantly through the skin
options.D: Sedatives consistently increase blood pressure and heart rate over time

explanation: Patients can drift easily from peaceful sleep into dangerously slow breathing. That is why watching them closely is a vital part of keeping them safe! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h1)

question: A patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) reports difficulty starting urination. Which anatomical structure is most likely causing this issue?

options.A: Seminal vesicle
options.B: Bulbourethral gland
options.C: Scrotal septum
options.D: Prostate gland

explanation: An enlarged prostate surrounds the urethral canal and compresses it, leading to urinary hesitancy and weak flow in BPH. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h8)

question: Which duty can a home health aide safely perform for a client?

options.A: Adjusting the dosage of high blood pressure medication
options.B: Administering prescribed intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Evaluating the healing progress of a surgical wound
options.D: Assisting with personal hygiene and bathing

explanation: Home health aides are trained to help with activities of daily living, such as bathing, grooming, and basic personal care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: A patient on chemotherapy has a very low white blood cell count. What should be your top nursing priority?

options.A: Administering high doses of oral iron supplements
options.B: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to combat fatigue
options.C: Preparing the patient for immediate surgical tumor removal
options.D: Protecting the patient from potential sources of infection

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! White blood cells are our body's soldiers. When their count drops (neutropenia), our main job is to guard the patient fiercely against any germs and infections.

question: Why is staff health education an important duty for the community health nurse?

options.A: It ensures teachers can prescribe antibiotics without seeing a doctor
options.B: It allows nursery workers to officially diagnose complex pediatric diseases
options.C: It replaces the need for any professional medical supervision in the community
options.D: It equips caregivers to properly recognize early signs of illness and prevent outbreaks

explanation: Educating caregivers helps them spot warning signs quickly and apply correct sanitation measures to protect the children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: Why is a nurse considered the final safety net during medication administration?

options.A: Because patients refuse to take medications unless handed by a nurse
options.B: Because doctors do not understand the pharmacology of prescribed drugs
options.C: Because they perform the final independent check before the drug enters the patient
options.D: Because hospital management shifts all legal penalties solely to the nursing staff

explanation: You are the last person to see the drug before it goes into the patient. Checking the order and dose one last time is your superpower for keeping patients safe!

question: What is a hapten?

options.A: A specialized white blood cell that produces antibodies
options.B: A massive protein found exclusively in mammalian red blood cells
options.C: A small molecule that needs a carrier to trigger an immune response
options.D: A complex hormone released during severe systemic inflammation

explanation: Haptens are too tiny on their own to get the immune system's attention. They have to hitch a ride on a larger carrier protein first!

question: In pharmacology, what do we mean by the term 'pharmacokinetics'?

options.A: How drugs are manufactured in a lab
options.B: What a drug does to the body
options.C: What the body does to a drug
options.D: How diseases destroy medication inside cells

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as the journey the drug takes inside you! It looks at how your body handles the medicine through absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. You've got this!

question: A head nurse wants to know if a newly introduced fall-prevention bundle actually decreases patient falls over the next year on the surgical ward. Which action represents applying prospective thinking?

options.A: Implementing the bundle today and tracking fall rates prospectively over the coming year
options.B: Interviewing staff nurses about falls that occurred before they were born
options.C: Asking elderly patients to guess why they might fall in the future
options.D: Looking up incident reports from five years ago to see how many people slipped

explanation: Applying a measure today and observing future outcomes embodies the core methodology of prospective clinical research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is a common sign that a PAC patient might be struggling emotionally?

options.A: Asking excessive questions about discharge medications
options.B: Demanding an immediate discharge from the hospital
options.C: Avoiding eye contact and withdrawing from conversation
options.D: Laughing loudly with visiting family members

explanation: When someone is overwhelmed or anxious, they often pull back, stay quiet, and avoid looking you in the eye.

question: A mum says she cannot afford expensive imported foods sometimes shown in diet books. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell her to borrow money so she can buy foreign foods from the supermarket
options.B: Advise her to skip meals until she can afford the expensive recommended items
options.C: Show her how to combine local staples like beans, local fish, and green vegetables for good nutrition
options.D: Explain that diet does not matter as long as she takes her routine clinic drugs

explanation: You don't need fancy imported foods for a healthy pregnancy! Local foods like beans, fish, and greens give all the power nutrition needed.

question: A patient on a breathing machine (ventilator) is at high risk for which mouth problem?

options.A: Losing their sense of smell completely and forever
options.B: Sudden growth of wisdom teeth right at the back
options.C: Drooling because of too much natural saliva production
options.D: Fast plaque buildup and ventilator-associated pneumonia

explanation: You've got this! Because intubated patients cannot clean their own teeth and often have dry mouths, germs gather quickly and can travel down to cause pneumonia.

question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Testosterone

explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: A community health nurse notices many teens in her local area know nothing about birth control. What is her best first step?

options.A: Report all teenagers to the local police division for investigation
options.B: Establish an educational youth-friendly reproductive health club at the local center
options.C: Wait until patients present with complications before offering advice
options.D: Ban all public discussions regarding sexual health in schools

explanation: Creating safe, welcoming spaces gives adolescents the accurate facts they need to protect their health and futures. Great nursing initiative!

question: Why should you check if a patient has recently passed stool before giving a suppository?

options.A: Stool presence guarantees that the drug will be absorbed twice as fast
options.B: A full rectum can block the medication from contacting the mucosal wall
options.C: Bowel movements prevent the nurse from wearing disposable gloves
options.D: Empty bowels mean the patient is allergic to the prescribed drug

explanation: If the rectum is full of stool, the suppository won't touch the lining properly, reducing drug absorption.

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial warning sign of an ectopic pregnancy you must teach patients to report right away?

options.A: Mild generalized fatigue and mild morning nausea
options.B: Temporary swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Clear and painless watery vaginal discharge
options.D: One-sided sharp pelvic pain with abnormal spotting

explanation: Sharp pain on just one side of the lower belly, paired with unusual bleeding, is a major red flag for an ectopic pregnancy that needs urgent care.

question: What does the famous saying 'the dose makes the poison' mean?

options.A: Small amounts of deadly poisons are always beneficial for health
options.B: Any substance can become harmful if the amount taken is too large
options.C: Only synthetic chemicals manufactured in laboratories are truly toxic
options.D: The chemical structure of a drug changes once inside the human stomach

explanation: Even safe things like water can become dangerous if you take too much of them at once. Toxicity is all about the quantity!

question: What type of lubricant should always be used on a flatus tube before insertion?

options.A: Water-soluble lubricant
options.B: Sterile cooking oil
options.C: Petroleum-based jelly
options.D: Alcohol-based gel

explanation: Water-soluble lubricant is safe for mucous membranes and prevents trauma, unlike petroleum-based products which are harder to clear and can damage tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing nursing education updates in developing areas?

options.A: Resistance to change from traditional workers
options.B: An excess of state-of-the-art simulation equipment
options.C: Shortages of qualified academic teaching staff
options.D: Infrastructure deficits like erratic electricity

explanation: Correct! Schools usually suffer from a *lack* of modern equipment, not an excess of it.

question: How does community mobilisation directly support primary health care goals?

options.A: By building large tertiary teaching hospitals in every small town
options.B: By stopping patients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.C: By helping people manage preventable diseases and improve local sanitation
options.D: By replacing community health workers with paid international staff

explanation: Primary health care focuses on prevention and community-level action, which mobilisation directly achieves. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the most critical check a nurse must do before giving penicillin for the first time?

options.A: Measuring the patient head circumference
options.B: Checking for a history of drug allergies
options.C: Evaluating the patient visual acuity score
options.D: Assessing the patient daily fluid intake

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies. A patient with a severe penicillin allergy can crash quickly from anaphylaxis if you miss this step.

question: Why is the CSSD so important for infection control?

options.A: It breaks the chain of infection by providing sterile instruments
options.B: It administers routine vaccinations to hospital staff
options.C: It isolates patients with contagious airborne diseases
options.D: It monitors patient antibiotic resistance patterns daily

explanation: By making sure every tool is thoroughly decontaminated and germ-free, CSSD stops infections from spreading from one patient to another.

question: A patient recovering from an intentional overdose is now awake and stable. What nursing action is most important?

options.A: Restricting all family visits to punish the patient for the suicide attempt
options.B: Providing continuous observation and psychological support while keeping the environment safe
options.C: Avoiding any conversation about the incident to prevent embarrassment
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately with a prescription for sedatives

explanation: You've got this. Emotional support and a safe, watch-careful environment are vital for anyone recovering from self-harm.

question: When do accidental needle-stick injuries most frequently occur in clinical settings?

options.A: When storing unopened boxes of sterile syringes in the pharmacy
options.B: During the physical assessment of a newly admitted patient
options.C: While washing hands with soap and water before a procedure
options.D: While recapping used needles after giving an injection

explanation: Trying to put the cap back onto a used needle is a leading cause of accidental punctures in nursing practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient on long-term warfarin who loves green leafy vegetables?

options.A: Stop eating all green vegetables immediately to stay safe
options.B: Double your vegetable intake only on days you take extra medication
options.C: Eat a consistent amount of green vegetables every week without sudden big changes
options.D: Boil all green vegetables for two hours to destroy all vitamins

explanation: Consistency is key! Patients don't need to avoid greens completely; they just need to eat a steady amount each week so their INR levels stay stable.

question: What causes crackles (rales) to be heard during lung auscultation?

options.A: Fluid or secretions popping open collapsed alveoli
options.B: Air rushing through severely narrowed large bronchi
options.C: Air trapped in the upper respiratory tract
options.D: Inflamed pleural membranes rubbing against each other

explanation: Crackles occur when moisture or fluid causes tiny air sacs to snap open during inspiration. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient with terrible watery diarrhea has raw, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing care?

options.A: Apply a drying powder to absorb moisture and stop wiping
options.B: Scrub the irritated skin firmly with soap and a rough cloth
options.C: Leave the skin exposed to room air without any protection
options.D: Clean the area gently, dry it, and apply a barrier cream

explanation: You got it! Liquid stool is harsh on the skin. Clean gently and use a good barrier cream to protect raw areas from irritation.

question: Which of these is usually one of the very first warning signs that a patient is slipping into shock?

options.A: Restlessness and increased heart rate
options.B: Elevated blood pressure and flushed face
options.C: Slow, bounding pulse and warm skin
options.D: High urine output and deep sleep

explanation: When blood flow dips, the body panics a bit and pumps harder (tachycardia) while the brain gets restless from lack of oxygen. Always trust your instincts when a patient suddenly seems 'off'!

question: How does severe malnutrition with low blood protein (albumin) affect highly protein-bound drugs?

options.A: Kidneys flush the medication out immediately without any effect
options.B: The liver instantly destroys the drug before it reaches any target
options.C: More free drug is available in the blood, increasing toxicity risk
options.D: The drug binds tighter to tissues and never enters the bloodstream

explanation: Think of blood proteins like seats on a bus for drugs. If there aren't enough seats (albumin), more drugs float around freely in the blood, which can easily lead to an accidental overdose effect! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: Which schedule describes substances with NO accepted medical use and high abuse risk?

options.A: Schedule V
options.B: Schedule IV
options.C: Schedule I
options.D: Schedule II

explanation: Schedule I drugs are considered too dangerous and lack approved medical applications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why do resource-limited regions often report higher rates of patient harm?

options.A: Local doctors have less formal education than foreign doctors
options.B: Medical technology in these regions is too advanced to operate
options.C: Weak infrastructure and understaffed facilities hinder safe care
options.D: Patients in these areas refuse to take their prescribed drugs

explanation: When hospitals lack steady power, enough staff, or basic supplies, it becomes much easier for errors to slip through.

question: Your patient starts having trouble breathing and facial swelling right after a new IV antibiotic starts. What should you do first?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately and notify the doctor.
options.B: Give the patient a glass of water and tell them to rest.
options.C: Write an incident report for the pharmacy department.
options.D: Slow down the drip rate and wait to see if it stops.

explanation: Patient safety first! Always stop the offending drug right away to prevent things from getting worse before calling the doctor.

question: What can happen if ear drops are administered while they are too cold?

options.A: Infection of the outer ear
options.B: Dizziness and vertigo
options.C: Immediate hearing loss
options.D: Swelling of the earlobe

explanation: Cold liquid near the eardrum stimulates the inner ear balance centers, triggering sudden dizziness and nausea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why do non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like hypertension often go unnoticed for years?

options.A: Symptoms only appear after a person reaches retirement age
options.B: They develop silently in the body without immediate noticeable symptoms
options.C: Standard diagnostic laboratory tests cannot detect chronic illnesses early
options.D: Patients refuse to visit primary health centres for routine check-ups

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like high blood pressure creep up slowly without causing obvious pain or distress. That's why routine checks are so important for your patients.

question: Why do many patients with psychosis stop taking their antipsychotic drugs at home?

options.A: Pharmacies give out free drugs
options.B: Doctors prefer short-term use only
options.C: Unpleasant side effects
options.D: The medication cures the disease permanently

explanation: Spot on! Dealing with side effects like weight gain or feeling sluggish is tough, and it's the number one reason patients stop their meds.

question: What causes platelets to stick together and form a temporary plug at an injury site?

options.A: A sudden drop in the overall body temperature
options.B: Contact with exposed collagen and released chemical messengers
options.C: An increase in red blood cell production by the liver
options.D: The direct action of white blood cells on the vessel wall

explanation: When platelets touch exposed collagen under the damaged endothelium, they activate, change shape, and release chemicals that attract more platelets to build the plug. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: How does a person acquire natural active immunity?

options.A: By receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.B: By getting a standard routine vaccine at a clinic
options.C: By recovering from a natural live infection
options.D: By receiving an injection of manufactured antibodies

explanation: Natural active immunity develops when the body fights off a real, live pathogen and builds its own lasting memory cells. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h3)

question: What sign should a nurse watch for as a delayed allergic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.B: Loss of taste on the tongue
options.C: Skin rash, hives, or itching
options.D: Temporary extra hair growth

explanation: Sometimes allergies show up hours later. Watch out for rashes, hives, or itching so you can treat them early.

question: Why do healthcare workers often check serum prealbumin instead of albumin to track recent nutritional changes?

options.A: It measures total body fat instead of protein
options.B: It has a shorter half-life and responds faster
options.C: It is much cheaper to run in any lab
options.D: It never changes during an infection

explanation: Prealbumin leaves the body quicker, meaning it shows recent nutrition improvements or drops much faster than albumin.

question: When a person suddenly faces a scary or stressful situation, what is the first stage of the body's stress response called?

options.A: Alarm reaction
options.B: Exhaustion phase
options.C: Recovery period
options.D: Resistance stage

explanation: That sudden rush you feel when startled? That's the alarm reaction! It's your body's immediate fight-or-flight kick-start to help you handle sudden stress. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which two quick checks must a nurse do at every single antenatal visit?

options.A: Blood pressure and urine protein testing
options.B: Internal pelvic exam and ultrasound scan
options.C: Chest X-ray and sputum culture
options.D: Blood glucose and stool microscopy

explanation: Always check BP and urine! These simple routine tests are your best tools for catching early warning signs of pre-eclampsia.

question: What should you tell a patient who says they need their rescue SABA inhaler multiple times every day?

options.A: Stop taking the rescue inhaler immediately and switch to drinking warm water
options.B: Contact your healthcare provider because increased use suggests worsening disease control
options.C: Double your daily dose of long-acting medication to make up for the breakthrough symptoms
options.D: This is a normal expected outcome of long-term therapy that requires no action

explanation: If a rescue inhaler is needed constantly, it's a sign that the underlying condition isn't well controlled. The doctor needs to review and adjust their daily management plan.

question: Why do fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis) usually need oral pills instead of just a surface cream?

options.A: Topical creams cannot penetrate deeply enough through the hard nail plate
options.B: Fungi living in toenails are completely immune to all topical antifungal creams
options.C: Topical medications wash away too quickly from the foot due to sweat
options.D: Nail infections are always caused by systemic internal organ failure

explanation: Correct! The nail plate is thick and tough, acting like a shield that surface creams can't pass through. Pills are needed to reach the fungus from within.

question: Why do older adults frequently struggle with constipation?

options.A: Overactive muscular contractions in the stomach
options.B: Excessive production of digestive enzymes
options.C: Slower peristalsis and reduced intestinal motility
options.D: Rapid absorption of water in the upper bowel

explanation: Exactly! As the gut ages, its muscle contractions slow down. This gives the body more time to absorb water from waste, leading to hard, difficult stools.

question: Which main muscle forms the wall of the urinary bladder and stretches as it fills up with urine?

options.A: Trigone muscle
options.B: Detrusor muscle
options.C: Dartos muscle
options.D: Cremaster muscle

explanation: You've got this! The detrusor muscle is the big muscular wall of the bladder that stretches out nicely to hold urine until you're ready to go.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To shorten the dying process
options.B: To replace family caregiving
options.C: To cure terminal illnesses
options.D: To improve quality of life

explanation: Palliative care focuses primarily on relieving symptoms and stress to give the patient and family the best possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h1)

question: Which human infectious disease is the only one successfully eradicated globally so far?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Malaria
options.C: Measles
options.D: Smallpox

explanation: Correct! Through a massive worldwide vaccination campaign led by the WHO, smallpox was completely wiped out.

question: How does the lower oesophageal sphincter keep itself tightly closed to stop acid reflux?

options.A: By active mucus production sealing the lower mucosal folds together
options.B: Through intrinsic smooth muscle tone reinforced by the diaphragmatic crura
options.C: By voluntary contraction of skeletal muscle fibers wrapped around the hiatus
options.D: Through continuous parasympathetic stimulation sent by the glossopharyngeal nerve

explanation: You got it! It relies on its own natural muscle tension plus a helpful extra squeeze from the diaphragm opening it passes through.

question: Which model of adult day care focuses primarily on meals, recreation, and socialization without intensive health services?

options.A: Surgical model
options.B: Social model
options.C: Acute care model
options.D: Medical model

explanation: The social model is centered around community interaction, leisure activities, and basic supervision rather than active medical treatments. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which type of nutrient requires the most energy for the body to break down and process?

options.A: Dietary fats
options.B: Protein
options.C: Simple sugars
options.D: Water

explanation: Protein is tough work for the gut! It takes way more metabolic effort to process protein than it does for fats or simple carbs.

question: Why do many families continue traditional practices that might be harmful to health?

options.A: Desire to increase the local population size
options.B: Lack of available modern medical equipment
options.C: Deeply rooted cultural beliefs and social norms
options.D: Direct orders given by government health officials

explanation: You've got this! Communities often stick to these practices because they see them as treasured cultural heritage rather than health risks. Understanding this helps us care for them better.

question: Why is internal haemorrhage often harder to detect quickly than external haemorrhage?

options.A: Internal blood vessels do not contain red blood cells
options.B: The blood is hidden inside body cavities and tissues
options.C: Internal bleeding stops automatically without any medical help
options.D: The body instantly absorbs all escaped internal blood

explanation: Because the bleeding occurs within closed body spaces like the abdomen or chest, there is no visible sign on the skin surface. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h1)

question: A pregnant woman experiences chronic malnutrition late in pregnancy. Which nutrient transfer process is most likely to be affected first regarding fetal bone development?

options.A: Pinocytosis of maternal immunoglobulins
options.B: Active transport of minerals like calcium
options.C: Simple diffusion of respiratory oxygen
options.D: Facilitated diffusion of free water

explanation: Minerals like calcium require active transport mechanisms powered by energy to build up in the fetal skeleton, which can be strained under severe maternal nutritional deficits. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why is breaking any single link in the chain of infection effective?

options.A: It boosts the patient's natural red blood cell count
options.B: It stops the infectious cycle from continuing
options.C: It permanently destroys all bacteria in the room
options.D: It cures the underlying primary disease immediately

explanation: Because the chain relies on every link connecting, removing or blocking just one link halts the spread of germs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is unsafe when caring for a patient with an indwelling catheter?

options.A: Keeping the drainage bag below the level of the bladder
options.B: Cleaning the perineal area and catheter tubing daily
options.C: Disconnecting the tubing frequently to let the patient walk easier
options.D: Removing the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed

explanation: Never break that closed system! Opening the tubing lets bacteria waltz right into the urinary tract.

question: What is the most important ingredient for success in personal rehabilitation?

options.A: Frequent hospital admissions every month
options.B: Expensive imported assistive equipment
options.C: Active participation from the individual
options.D: Strict supervision by a medical doctor

explanation: A patient's own drive and willingness to try make the biggest difference in their recovery journey. You are their guide, but they do the heavy lifting!

question: A public health nurse wants to measure how many live births occurred per one thousand people in a town over one year. Which rate should be calculated?

options.A: Disease Prevalence Rate
options.B: Crude Birth Rate
options.C: Hospital Admission Ratio
options.D: Maternal Mortality Rate

explanation: The Crude Birth Rate specifically calculates live births per one thousand population in a defined one-year period. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a major challenge many healthcare facilities in Nigeria face when trying to dispose of waste?

options.A: Having too many modern autoclaves than needed
options.B: Excessive funding for environmental protection programs
options.C: Unreliable electricity supply that halts incinerator operations
options.D: Lack of any medical waste being generated in wards

explanation: Spot on! Frequent power cuts can shut down electrical incinerators and big sterilization machines, making safe waste management a real daily struggle.

question: Which hormone primarily stimulates sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Aldosterone

explanation: Aldosterone acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts to increase sodium and water reabsorption, raising blood volume. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To allow rapid absorption of testosterone directly into the skin
options.B: To keep the testicles cooler than body temperature for sperm production
options.C: To provide a direct connection to the external urinary meatus
options.D: To protect the reproductive organs from high intra-abdominal pressure

explanation: Sperm are sensitive! They need a slightly cooler temperature than the rest of the body to grow and develop properly, which is why the scrotum hangs outside.

question: What is the main duty of the anaesthetist during an operation?

options.A: Monitoring the patient's vital signs and managing pain
options.B: Transporting the patient safely from the ward to theatre
options.C: Documenting sponge and instrument counts every thirty minutes
options.D: Handing sterile instruments directly to the operating surgeon

explanation: The anaesthetist focuses entirely on keeping the patient asleep, stable, and pain-free while watching all life signs closely. They are the patient's guardian angels for comfort!

question: Which layer of the skin acts as the main shield blocking most drugs from easily entering the body?

options.A: Stratum corneum
options.B: Sweat gland ducts
options.C: Dermal blood vessels
options.D: Subcutaneous fat layer

explanation: The stratum corneum is the tough outer layer of your epidermis that naturally keeps foreign substances out. Great job remembering your anatomy!

question: A primary nurse notices a prescribed drug dose does not match a patient's failing kidneys. What is the best action?

options.A: Wait until the next shift change to let the incoming nurse deal with it.
options.B: Advocate for the patient by contacting the physician to question the safe dosage.
options.C: Administer the medication anyway since the doctor prescribed it.
options.D: Stop all nursing documentation for the day to avoid liability.

explanation: You are the patient's safety net! Always speak up and check with the doctor if a medication dose looks unsafe for your patient's lab results.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if a patient starts showing signs of an allergic rash after an injection?

options.A: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the rash disappears on its own
options.B: Ask the patient to write down her personal medical history
options.C: Stop the drug administration immediately and provide emergency care
options.D: Transfer the patient to a pharmacy for a replacement drug

explanation: Safety first! Always stop the medication right away to prevent any further reaction, then jump into emergency care.

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood glucose
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: You got it! Serum albumin is a classic protein marker we use to check a surgical patient's nutritional reserves.

question: How does washing your hands thoroughly break the chain of infection?

options.A: It removes the susceptible host entirely
options.B: It eliminates the initial reservoir
options.C: It stops the mode of transmission
options.D: It destroys the infectious agent completely

explanation: Hand hygiene removes germs from your hands, preventing them from traveling from one patient or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: What color do Gram-positive bacteria show up as under the microscope after a Gram stain?

options.A: Blue
options.B: Green
options.C: Pink
options.D: Purple

explanation: Gram-positive bacteria have thick cell walls that proudly trap that bright purple crystal violet dye. Easy to remember: P for Positive and Purple!

question: A patient comes in with a suspected paracetamol overdose. Which LFT enzyme results will you expect to shoot up first?

options.A: Albumin and total protein
options.B: ALT and AST
options.C: Amylase and lipase
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

explanation: Well done! Too much paracetamol causes sudden injury to liver cells, spilling intracellular enzymes like ALT and AST quickly into the bloodstream.

question: When is the best time for a pregnant woman to come in for her first booking visit?

options.A: Right after active labor begins
options.B: During the first trimester
options.C: During the final postpartum month
options.D: Only at week thirty-six

explanation: Getting her in during the first trimester lets you set a solid health baseline right from the start and catch any early risks.

question: What is the main job of flat bones in the body?

options.A: Absorbing high impact forces in tight spaces like the wrist
options.B: Acting as long levers to propel the body forward during running
options.C: Guiding tendons smoothly across major joints without friction
options.D: Protecting internal organs and providing broad muscle attachment sites

explanation: Flat bones (like your skull and sternum) act like helmets and shields for vital organs while giving muscles a wide place to anchor.

question: What major nutrient do legumes like cowpeas (beans) and bambara groundnuts bring to our local pots?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Saturated animal fats
options.C: Plant-based protein
options.D: Simple sugars

explanation: Exactly right! Legumes and beans are fantastic, budget-friendly sources of protein, especially when meat isn't within reach.

question: If household incomes in a community suddenly increase, what change in healthcare use are we likely to see?

options.A: An increase in the uptake of elective and preventive health services
options.B: A total cessation of visits to traditional local healers
options.C: No alteration in how residents access local health clinics
options.D: A sharp decrease in the number of emergency room admissions

explanation: Spot on! When people have more money in their pockets, they can finally afford wellness checks, vitamins, and elective care before emergencies happen.

question: A resident is scheduled for discharge next month. What should the care team arrange before departure?

options.A: Termination of all follow-up medical care
options.B: Immediate readmission to an acute psychiatric ward
options.C: Outpatient therapy appointments and secure housing
options.D: A police record check for employment eligibility

explanation: Wonderful! Good discharge planning means setting up safe housing and ongoing outpatient support beforehand to ensure a smooth transition and prevent relapse.

question: Why is reproductive health nursing considered a sensitive area of care?

options.A: It involves more paperwork than other clinical departments
options.B: It deals with deeply personal aspects tied to self-image and culture
options.C: Medical treatments for these conditions are always experimental
options.D: Patients are rarely willing to talk about their symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Reproductive health touches on private parts of life, culture, and identity. Showing extra empathy and privacy goes a long way.

question: During a health emergency, how do health ministries use surveillance data?

options.A: To allocate scarce medical resources where they are needed most
options.B: To select which nursing students receive scholarships
options.C: To decide which private hospitals should be closed permanently
options.D: To determine salary increases for hospital administrators

explanation: Good data shows us exactly where an outbreak is hitting hardest. That way, we can rush medications, supplies, and staff right where they'll save the most lives.

question: Why must an educator look at learner characteristics when picking a teaching method?

options.A: First-year students and advanced trainees require different levels of structure and guidance
options.B: Advanced learners already know all practical procedures before entering nursing school
options.C: School accreditation bodies dictate that every year must use a single fixed method
options.D: Students will refuse to attend class if they do not choose their own teaching style

explanation: Fresh first-year students need more step-by-step guidance and support, whereas senior students are usually ready for independent problem-solving.

question: What makes a longitudinal research design special?

options.A: Collecting data from the same participants repeatedly over time
options.B: Testing a new drug without telling the patients
options.C: Comparing two different hospitals during the same month
options.D: Surveying a large group of patients just once

explanation: Spot on! Longitudinal studies are great because they follow the exact same group of people and measure things on multiple occasions to see how they change.
